system_description.narrative_title: Trump–Putin diesel deal and its geopolitical fallout
system_description.narrative_summary: A bilateral agreement brokered by the U.S. president to open Russian diesel to global markets has become the focal point of a wider system of destabilizing feedbacks: bipartisan political backlash, strains on intelligence and military cooperation with Ukraine, and incentives for Moscow to sustain or escalate military pressure. The energy diplomacy interacts with defence technology controls (Starlink/Starshield), NATO cohesion, and global fuel markets to produce cascading operational, political and economic effects that risk further allied fragmentation and renewed strikes.
system_description.scope: The system includes U.S.-Russia energy diplomacy (diesel/oil deals), the Russia–Ukraine military conflict (strikes on refineries, data centres, ships), Western political and parliamentary responses (U.S. Congress, EU leaders, NATO), intelligence and satellite/service restrictions affecting Ukrainian operations (Starlink/Starshield), and short-term global fuel market flows and maritime security incidents.
system_description.super_system: The global security–economic order: international geopolitics, alliance politics, and energy markets
adjacent_subsystems: NATO alliance cohesion and collective defence planning
Domestic political systems in the US and Europe (congresses, elections, public opinion)

variables.name: Diesel export flow
variables.description: Volume of diesel moved from suppliers into international markets per unit time.

variables.name: Global fuel price level
variables.description: Average market price for refined fuels that influences economic and policy decisions across markets.

variables.name: Strikes on energy infrastructure rate
variables.description: Frequency of kinetic or sabotage attacks targeting fuel production, refining, storage or distribution assets per unit time.

variables.name: Maritime security incident rate
variables.description: Rate of hostile or disruptive incidents affecting commercial and military shipping in relevant sea lanes.

variables.name: Allied cohesion level
variables.description: Aggregate degree of political and operational alignment among partner actors on strategy and burden-sharing.

variables.name: Intensity of intelligence sharing
variables.description: Volume and regularity of actionable intelligence exchanged between partners for operational use.

variables.name: Defence technology control extent
variables.description: Scope and restrictiveness of policies and controls limiting transfer and use of military-relevant technologies.

variables.name: Domestic political backlash intensity
variables.description: Strength of domestic political opposition and public sentiment against a given external policy action.

variables.name: Military pressure intensity
variables.description: Scale and tempo of forces and operations exerting coercive pressure on opposing forces or territories.

variables.name: Sanctions enforcement strictness
variables.description: Degree to which economic restrictions and compliance measures are applied and monitored to limit economic activity.

variables.name: Energy supply chain disruption level
variables.description: Extent to which production, transport and distribution of fuels are obstructed, delayed or degraded.

variables.name: Military satellite communications availability
variables.description: Accessibility and capacity of satellite-based communications and data services for military or tactical operations.

variables.name: Intelligence timeliness
variables.description: Latency between observation/collection and delivery of actionable intelligence to operational users.

variables.name: Legislative countermeasure pressure
variables.description: Momentum and frequency of legislative and parliamentary initiatives aimed at reversing or constraining policies.

variables.name: Incentives for hostile escalation
variables.description: Net political, economic and military incentives that increase the probability of escalation by an actor.

variables.name: Fuel flow rerouting rate
variables.description: Speed at which fuel shipments and trade routes are reconfigured in response to supply, price or security changes.

catalysts.title: Ukraine resumes strikes on Russian refineries
catalysts.description: Kyiv's announced resumption of attacks on Russian refineries begins an active campaign degrading Russian fuel infrastructure and exports.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Ukraine to resume strikes on Russian refineries", "Ukraine Resumes Strikes On Russian Refineries", Zelenskyy statements.

catalysts.title: Russia restarts diesel exports after Trump deal
catalysts.description: Kremlin statements that Russia has restarted diesel shipments — and may exceed volumes announced under the Trump–Putin agreement — increase available supply flows.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Kremlin says Russia restarts diesel exports after deal with Trump", "Russia says its diesel exports may exceed volumes announced by Trump".

catalysts.title: Curtailment of Starshield/Starlink military services
catalysts.description: Reported limits, speed caps and policy restraints on SpaceX's military-grade services reduce Ukraine's satcom capacity and timely intelligence flows.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Ukraine says SpaceX limits Starlink operations", "Elon Musk says Trump is 'ultimately' responsible"; US intelligence sharing threats.

catalysts.title: Legislative and allied political pressure over diesel deal
catalysts.description: Bipartisan domestic opposition and allied criticism trigger hearings, legal scrutiny and parliamentary initiatives to constrain or review the deal.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Trump defends Russia diesel deal after bipartisan pushback", "More Republicans come out against Trump's diesel deal", legality questions.

catalysts.title: Spike in maritime attacks in Black Sea and NATO waters
catalysts.description: Recent sinkings, fires and suspected strikes on commercial ships indicate a continuing rise in hostile maritime incidents affecting regional sea lanes.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Russia suspected of striking two tankers in Nato waters", "Two ships ablaze in Romanian Black Sea waters", drone-sinking reports.

catalysts.title: NATO increases defensive posture and funds drone-defence tech
catalysts.description: NATO commanders' warnings and a targeted fund for drone defence drive shifts in deployments, capabilities and alliance operational focus.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "NATO fund targets drone defence technologies", "NATO’s Top Commander Lays Out Plan to Thwart a Russian Attack".

catalysts.title: US floats unfreezing some Russian assets to restart talks
catalysts.description: Reports that Washington may unfreeze some Russian assets as a bargaining move to restart peace negotiations could alter sanction enforcement dynamics.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "US floats unfreezing some Russian assets to restart Ukraine peace talks".

catalysts.title: Russian expansion of drone attack bases
catalysts.description: Satellite imagery of a major new Russian drone attack base signals growing strike capacity against energy and regional targets.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "Russia builds major new drone attack base in six weeks", plus recent drone/refinery attack reports.
